About Last Mile Delivery

Walmart Last Mile Delivery is responsible for building and operating the capabilities that connect customers with their orders during the final stage of the delivery journey.

A critical part of this ecosystem is Spark Driver, Walmart’s platform connecting independent drivers with delivery opportunities. Providing a reliable driver experience requires coordination across product, engineering, operations, analytics, communications, and support teams to ensure that new capabilities are tested effectively, launched safely, monitored in real time, and quickly improved when issues arise.

- How a large-scale gig delivery platform attracts, engages, and retains drivers

- How loyalty and rewards programs can influence user behavior and engagement

- How strategic concepts are tested, prioritized, and translated into an actionable roadmap

- Curiosity about consumer behavior, loyalty, marketplaces, gig economy platforms, or digital products

- Ability to structure and solve ambiguous problems

- Strong written, verbal, and executive communication skills

- Collaboration-first working style with the ability to work across multiple functions

- Innovation-driven mindset and interest in developing new customer or user experiences

- Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment

About the Team

The Autonomous Vehicle (AV) Engineering organization supports the development of safe, reliable, and high-performing assisted and automated driving systems throughout the vehicle lifecycle. Our teams combine vehicle systems expertise, engineering analysis, data, hands-on execution, and disciplined documentation to accelerate learning and enable productive development testing.

The Fleet Reliability Engineering and AV Test Engineering teams work closely with AV Operations, Service Operations, technicians, vehicle integration, software, systems, safety, and supplier teams. Together, they identify risks, plan and execute validation, analyze vehicle and fleet performance, resolve issues, and improve the processes that keep development vehicles safe, available, serviceable, and ready for testing.

We are hiring interns across two complementary focus areas. Both opportunities offer hands-on experience with autonomous vehicle development, cross-functional problem-solving, data analysis, scripting, and real-world engineering execution.

What You Will Do

Fleet Reliability Engineering

The Fleet Reliability Engineering team improves the health, availability, serviceability, and operational readiness of autonomous vehicle fleets.

- Define and improve fleet health, reliability, availability, uptime, and serviceability metrics.
- Analyze vehicle health data, telemetry, diagnostic information, service records, work orders, incidents, and operational data.
- Support dashboards, data-mining activities, and analytics that provide visibility into fleet condition and reliability trends.
- Investigate recurring vehicle, hardware, software, sensor, electrical, or operational issues by organizing symptoms, timelines, configurations, and supporting evidence.
- Support root-cause investigations, issue prioritization, corrective-action tracking, and communication of findings to technical and operational stakeholders.
- Partner with technicians and service teams to evaluate repairs, maintenance activities, return-to-service requirements, and opportunities to improve repeatability.
- Develop standard work, checklists, troubleshooting guides, and documentation that improve fleet reliability, service execution, and issue closure.
- Develop scripting and analysis tools to automate data processing, fleet reporting, reliability calculations, and engineering workflows.
- Support reliability testing and validation activities using vehicles, benches, diagnostic tools, simulation, and available fleet data.

AV Test Engineering

The AV Test Engineering team plans, executes, and analyzes testing of assisted and automated driving capabilities across simulation, benches, closed courses, and on-road development fleets.

- Translate engineering questions, feature requirements, and test requests into clear test cases, procedures, and acceptance criteria.
- Assess test feasibility and identify dependencies, including vehicles, routes, prototypes, software branches, tools, instrumentation, safety coverage, staffing, and operating approvals.
- Prepare and execute feature, sensor-level, system-level, regression, A/B comparison, and vehicle-level tests.
- Execute performance and validation tests using simulation, playback, bench, HIL/SIL, closed-course, and on-road fleets.
- Develop scripts to automate testing, data collection, result processing, and repeatable test workflows in vehicles and on benches.
- Analyze vehicle, sensor, software, and system data to evaluate performance, identify regressions, and improve validation efficiency.
- Document test results, consolidate findings, create defects or mitigations, and support root-cause investigations and re-test plans.
- Support the creation of test datasets, scenario libraries, regression suites, dashboards, and automated test pipelines.
- Coordinate with AV Operations and cross-functional engineering teams to schedule and execute testing safely and consistently.

Tech & Data Program Summer 2027 – Data Engineer Intern

Program Overview

At The Hartford, we foster an inclusive and collaborative environment where every voice is valued and every idea can make an impact. Our culture is built on integrity, innovation, and a customer-first mindset. We believe in empowering employees to grow through continuous learning, mentorship, meaningful work, and opportunities to contribute to solutions that support our customers and business.

As a Data Engineer Intern, you will help build and support the data pipelines, platforms, and processes that enable analytics, reporting, automation, and AI-driven insights across the organization. This role is ideal for students who are interested in building the systems behind the data — transforming raw information into reliable, usable data assets that help teams make better decisions.

Bring your curiosity, technical mindset, and willingness to learn. Your voice and perspective matter here.

About the Experience

The Hartford’s Technology, Data, AI, and Operations organization offers an immersive summer internship program designed to help students explore career paths in technology, data engineering, cybersecurity, AI, analytics, data science, and technology operations within the insurance industry.

As part of The Hartford’s growing investment in AI and advanced analytics, interns will explore how emerging technologies — including generative AI, machine learning, and automation — are transforming business operations, decision-making, and customer experience.

In this role, you will gain hands-on experience supporting data solutions that help power business insights, analytics products, and future AI capabilities.

This role is a hybrid position in Chicago, IL. Candidate must be authorized to work in the US without company sponsorship. The company will not support the STEM OPT I-983 Training Plan endorsement for this position.

What You'll Gain

- Hands-on experience designing, building, and supporting data pipelines and data workflows
- Exposure to modern data engineering practices, including ETL/ELT, data transformation, data quality, and cloud-based data platforms
- Opportunities to work with tools and technologies such as Python, SQL, PL/SQL, Snowflake, GitHub, and cloud platforms
- Exposure to how data engineering enables analytics, reporting, automation, machine learning, and AI use cases
- Mentorship, coaching, feedback, and self-directed learning opportunities
- Networking, volunteerism, and employee engagement experiences with peers and leaders across the organization
- A stronger understanding of how data supports decision-making within the insurance industry

Ways You'll Learn, Grow, and Contribute

Depending on your role and project assignments, your experience may include:

- Build and support data pipelines that ingest, transform, and prepare data for business and analytical use
- Work with structured and unstructured data to enable analytics, reporting, and AI-driven solutions
- Apply data engineering tools and techniques (e.g., Python, SQL, ETL processes, cloud technologies) to develop reliable data assets
- Ensure data quality, consistency, and performance through profiling, validation, and monitoring activities
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to deliver scalable data solutions that address business needs
- Leverage AI tools (e.g., Copilot) to enhance productivity and support the development of data solutions that power advanced analytics and machine learning

Required Qualifications

- Undergraduate or graduate student expecting to graduate in May 2028 with a Bachelor's or Master's degree and a GPA of 3.0 or higher
- Pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, IT, Management Information Systems, Data Analytics, Applied Mathematics, or another STEM-related field
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills
- Strong communication, collaboration, and interpersonal skills
- Curiosity and willingness to explore new technologies and challenge assumptions
- Demonstrated ability to analyze complex problems using structured thinking and logical reasoning
- Commitment to ethical judgment, responsible data use, and understanding how technology decisions affect stakeholders and the business

Experience and exposure to some or all of the following:

- Programming & Querying: Python, SQL, PL/SQL
- Data Engineering: ETL/ELT, data pipelines, data transformation, data profiling, data quality, data modeling
- Data Platforms & Tools: Snowflake, GitHub, relational databases, data warehouse concepts
- Cloud Technologies: AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud
- Analytics & BI: Tableau, dashboards, reporting, data mining, or business intelligence tools
- AI & Emerging Technology: Familiarity with AI/ML concepts, generative AI tools, LLMs, NLP, or interest in building data foundations that support AI-driven solutions
- Agile Ways of Working: Exposure to Agile teams, sprint delivery, or collaborative product-based work

Our internship program is designed as a pipeline for future full-time opportunities. High-performing interns may be considered for full-time roles within The Hartford’s Technology & Data organization.
